subject: Social Media
title: Iran's Green Movement
description: A fast breakdown of Iran's Green Movement for builders.

hook.text: In 2009, Iranians flooded the streets after a disputed election. Twitter became their megaphone to the world.

buildup.text: Protesters tweeted locations, shared videos, and coordinated marches. Western media called it the Twitter Revolution.

discovery.text: The regime crushed the movement. Tweets didn't stop bullets. Most coordination happened by phone and word of mouth.

twist.text: Iran then built one of the world's most advanced internet filters. The uprising taught them what to fear.

climax.text: The 'Twitter Revolution' label was mostly Western media hype. Only 0.027% of Iranians used Twitter in 2009.

punchline.text: The revolution was real. The Twitter part was myth.

quiz.question: What percentage of Iranians actually used Twitter during the 2009 protests?
